alerts.reason: Reported sales growth fell 4.28 percentage points, from +3.82% year over year in June to -0.47% in September. Extending that pace gives approximately -4.75% in December and -9.03% in March, placing the forecast crossing in the target quarter. The timing rests on the two sales observations.

Reported net sales went from -0.12% year over year in June to -2.24% in September. A similar pace implies about -4.36% in December and -6.48% in March. Lower volume drove the September decline despite higher customer pricing, and the Taunton and Irvine closures contributed to the volume loss (A, C).

Net sales fell 3.84% year over year in September after growing 9.99% in June (A and sales history). The $614.7 million September backlog could support December shipments, but it was $354.3 million smaller than a year earlier. With fewer orders available for later shipment, I forecast December above -5% and a March decline of at least 5% (B, C).

Reported revenue fell 4.31% year over year in June and 4.15% in September. Those similar readings support a December forecast above -5%. Lower shipment volume (C) and reduced consumer spending (B) leave room for the March decline to deepen by the 0.86 percentage points needed to cross from September's rate.

The reported revenue decline narrowed from 3.01% in June to 1.19% in September, supporting a December forecast above -5% (A and sales history). Less available freight and exposure to spot rates pushed One-Way Truckload revenue per mile excluding fuel surcharge down 4.8%. Continued pressure on both rates and loads supports a consolidated revenue decline of at least 5% in March (B, D).

Total revenue growth slowed from +4.72% year over year in June to +0.15% in September. Passenger miles rose 5.2%, barely offsetting a 4.8% fall in passenger yield, while cargo revenue fell 30.9% (A, B). A repeat of the 4.57-point slowdown would leave December above -5%. Further yield pressure would put March below the threshold.

Consolidated revenue growth slowed from +6.77% year over year in June to +0.39% in September. An 11% increase in passenger traffic offset a 10% yield decline as demand softened (B). I forecast traffic growth will still cushion December revenue enough to stay above -5%, but that the offset will weaken enough for a March decline of at least 5%.
